skill.name: google-agents-cli-deploy
skill.description: Guide Google ADK agent deployments to Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE with CI/CD, secrets, service accounts, testing, rollback, and troubleshooting guidance.
skill.summary: Deploy Google ADK agents across Google Cloud targets with production-ready operational guidance.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: Static findings are almost entirely false positives from Markdown examples, placeholder URLs, localhost testing commands, and documented Google Cloud deployment workflows. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden executable code was found. One medium semantic risk remains because the troubleshooting guide recommends forced Terraform state unlock without safety checks.

remediation.issue: Terraform force-unlock guidance lacks a safety warning.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to confirm no active Terraform run owns the lock before using force-unlock, and prefer resolving the stuck process first.

remediation.issue: Secret examples use API key placeholders in shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder values clearly fake and remind users not to paste real secrets into shared shells or logs.

remediation.issue: Deployment commands can modify live Google Cloud resources.
remediation.suggestion: Retain the explicit human approval requirement before running deploy, infrastructure, rollback, or IAM-changing commands.

content.value_statement: Deploying ADK agents across Google Cloud targets requires many infrastructure choices. This skill guides target selection, deployment commands, secrets, CI/CD, testing, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Compare Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE deployment targets for ADK agents.
Guide agents-cli deployment workflows with approval checkpoints and status recovery.
Explain service accounts, IAM roles, Secret Manager access, and required Google Cloud APIs.
Provide CI/CD, rollback, and troubleshooting guidance for production deployments.
Show testing patterns for deployed agents using agents-cli, curl, and Google Cloud credentials.
limitations: Requires an existing or scaffolded Google ADK agent project.
Does not replace Google Cloud permissions review or infrastructure approval.
Focuses on Google Cloud targets, not other hosting providers.
Some actions can create or modify billable cloud resources.

use_cases.title: Choose a deployment target
use_cases.description: Compare Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE based on networking, scaling, sessions, and operational control.

use_cases.title: Deploy with safer operations
use_cases.description: Use approval checkpoints, dry runs, service accounts, and Secret Manager patterns before changing cloud resources.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers managing Google Cloud deployments

use_cases.title: Recover a failed deployment
use_cases.description: Troubleshoot IAM, Cloud SQL, secret access, logging, rollback, and pending Agent Runtime operations.

prompt_templates.title: Pick my target
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE for my ADK agent. Ask what you need before recommending a target.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a dev deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ADK project and prepare the steps to deploy it to dev with agents-cli. Do not run deployment commands without my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Configure production CI/CD
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production CI/CD setup for this ADK agent, including service accounts, required APIs, secrets, staging, and approval gates.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot deployment failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this failed ADK deployment. Check IAM, service account impersonation, Secret Manager access, logs, rollback options, and pending operations.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy an ADK agent with private networking and managed sessions.
output_examples.output: A target recommendation with tradeoffs, required flags, service account notes, and a confirmation checkpoint before deployment.

output_examples.input: My Cloud Run agent returns 403 during testing.
output_examples.output: A focused troubleshooting checklist covering authentication headers, IAP, IAM bindings, and log locations.

output_examples.input: Set up CI/CD for staging and production.
output_examples.output: A staged implementation plan covering runner choice, Workload Identity Federation, secrets, approval gates, and rollback paths.

best_practices: Ask for explicit human approval before running deploy, infrastructure, IAM, or rollback commands.
Use Secret Manager for credentials instead of plain environment variables or checked-in files.
Start with dry runs and dev deployments before enabling production CI/CD.
anti_patterns: Running agents-cli deploy without confirming the target project, region, and service account.
Creating production resources manually when Terraform should manage the infrastructure.
Treating placeholder secret commands as a place to paste real credentials into logs or shared terminals.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy the agent automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to ask for explicit approval before running deployment commands.

faq.question: Which Google Cloud targets are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Agent Runtime, Cloud Run, and GKE for Google ADK agents.

faq.question: Can it help with CI/CD setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for runners, Workload Identity Federation, staging, production approval, and pipeline troubleshooting.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: The skill recommends Google Secret Manager and service account access instead of storing raw secrets in source code.

faq.question: Does it support non-Google Cloud providers?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is specific to Google Cloud deployment targets and Google ADK tooling.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot deployed agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers IAM errors, secret access, Cloud SQL permissions, logs, timeouts, and rollback options.
